title: Fuchsian groups and orbifold Riemann surfaces, Part II: Nielsen cores and quadratic-class surfaces
summary: Build the missing finite-area Nielsen cores of finitely generated Fuchsian groups of the second kind, then construct the bordered orbifolds attached to real quadratic narrow ideal classes. Their continued-fraction polygons give exact signatures, lengths and areas. Cusp-normalized conformal rigidity recovers the class, while multiplicity-preserving measures and truncated Stokes provide the geometric input to arithmetic equidistribution.
readme: The parent supplies effective actions, ordinary quotient charts, polygons, cusps and cofinite signatures. This Part II adds geodesic boundary and arithmetic cores. Its full companion reader pins every target, API, example, source locator and proof repair. The independent Bakker–Tsimerman volume/gonality continuation already belongs to HyperbolicCurveVolumesAndGonality and is imported by ownership, never duplicated. All statements are planning targets; the compact suggested file contains only light definitions and milestones statable at the baseline pins.

stages.title: Nielsen regions and bordered signatures
stages.description: For a nonelementary discrete subgroup of PSL₂(ℝ), define its limit set in the full ideal circle, the closed hyperbolic hull and its orbifold quotient. Prove geometric finiteness for finitely generated groups, identify funnels and their primitive boundary axes, construct the finite signature (g;m₁,…,mᵣ;s;t), and derive area=2π(2g−2+s+t+Σ(1−1/mⱼ)) from polygon Gauss–Bonnet. Boundary means actual geodesic boundary; paired polygon edges and cusp truncation curves are excluded. Include the first-kind comparison with the parent’s cofinite case.

stages.title: Quadratic cycles and their Ford polygons
stages.description: Import the primitive reduced minus cycle of a narrow class A of positive fundamental discriminant D. For Nₖ=Σⱼ≤ₖnⱼ and m=Nℓ, construct Sₖ=T^NₖST^−Nₖ, Γ_A=⟨S₁,…,Sℓ,T^m⟩ and its strip outside the unit discs. Verify side identifications, the free product ℤ*(C₂)^*ℓ, full cusp stabilizer ⟨T^m⟩, cyclic-rotation conjugacy, endpoint inequalities and γ_w=S₁⋯SℓT^m. Prove second kind and infinite index using a nonempty free ideal interval, not an invalid converse from infinite index alone.

stages.title: The arithmetic core and its boundary
stages.description: Carry out the finite-arc cutting algorithm with its disjoint-disc endpoint induction. Construct F_A as the quotient of C(Λ_A) by Γ_A and the map to the modular orbifold. Identify signature (0;2 repeated ℓ_A;1;1), a simple primitive oriented boundary projecting to the parametrized C_A, length 2log ε_D and area πℓ_A. Record distances 2arsinh(n/2) between chosen height-one lifts without interpreting them as intrinsic cone-point distances. Use D=12 and D=28 as signature, length and lift-spacing tests; the complete worked example, including covering multiplicities, is in N.4.

stages.title: Conformal recovery of the narrow class
stages.description: Double the bordered core across its analytic geodesic boundary with cone orders retained. Prove that an orientation-preserving conformal orbifold equivalence lifts to a PSL₂(ℝ) conjugacy. Normalize the unique cusp to ∞, identify the maximal-height elliptic lifts Nₖ+mℤ+i, force the dilation to equal one, and recover the cyclic digit sequence from their successive gaps. Conclude, for a fixed real quadratic field, that the conformal orbifold class of F_A determines A.

stages.title: Core measures and complementary coverings
stages.description: Push the finite upstairs core measure to the modular orbifold, retaining all multiplicities. Define normalized finite-family and genus probability measures. Prove ν_A+ν_{JA⁻¹}=3(ℓ_A+ℓ_{JA⁻¹})μ_mod as an equality of measures, including self-intersections and reciprocal boundaries. Deduce exact modular probability for the whole narrow class group, any genus when J is a square, and an individual class with A²=J. The asymptotic equidistribution theorem remains with GN.4. Work D=12 and D=28 explicitly, including complementary multiplicities 9 and 21.

stages.title: Cusp-truncated Stokes and spectral inputs
stages.description: Construct height truncations of the actual core polygon and their oriented boundary bookkeeping. For C² Γ_A-invariant F with −y²(F_xx+F_yy)=λF and vanishing horizontal ∂z flux, prove existence of the height-truncated integral and (λ/2)I_A(F)=∮∂F_A i∂zF dz. Give the L¹ version and the level-one Maass/Eisenstein critical-line specializations from AS Fourier and differentiated cusp inputs; replace the boundary by C_A only for full modular invariance. Import ordinary/corners Stokes from current DifferentialGeometry Layer 5.
